Senate leaves CLARITY Act off Monday’s floor plan.



Monday’s schedule lists only a spending-bill vote, with no H.R. 3633 or Digital Asset Market Clarity Act action. That does not kill the crypto market-structure bill, but it leaves leaders without a publicly listed floor path.

The Details: 

•	Floor path: A future CLARITY motion to proceed would require a separate cloture process unless leaders use unanimous consent or another expedited procedure.

•	Faster path: A special bipartisan petition can shorten the process if it has the required 16 signers. 

•	Alternate path: A unanimous-consent agreement could compress the schedule, but any senator can object.

Goldman Sachs warned that reducing Federal Reserve policy guidance could increase market volatility, pricing errors, and delays in monetary-policy transmission.

The Details:

•	Market signals: Goldman said giving markets less insight into the Fed’s reaction function could increase pricing errors.

•	Policy impact: The bank said reduced guidance would not improve policymaker feedback.

•	Transmission risk: Goldman said the approach could delay how quickly monetary policy affects financial conditions.

•	Volatility concern: The bank said less clarity could create unnecessary volatility across financial markets.

New York Fed President John Williams said current policy remains well positioned to return inflation to the Fed’s 2% target.

The Details:

•	FOMC decision: Williams strongly supported the latest policy decision.

•	Inflation response: He said the Fed would act if inflation progress stalls.

•	Middle East prices: Williams expects Middle East-driven price pressures to fade.

•	AI investment: He said AI investment does not currently pose a financial-stability threat.

$UPST reported $1.397 billion in July loan originations, or about $51.0 million per day, while its Upstart Macro Index rose to 1.50 from 1.49.

The Details:

•	Origination volume: July originations totaled $1.397 billion.

•	Daily pace: The reported volume equated to approximately $51.0 million per day.

•	Macro index: UMI increased to 1.50, its highest reading since January 2026.

•	Credit risk: Upstart said UMI remains above its long-term baseline, signaling elevated macro-driven default risk.
$BOW American Family to Acquire Bowhead Specialty in $1.2 Billion Transaction

$ACHR said its piloted Midnight aircraft completed a Salinas–Monterey roundtrip in coordination with the FAA, with each leg taking about nine minutes.

The Details:

•	Route test: The flight connected Salinas and Monterey, a trip Archer said typically takes more than 35 minutes by car.

•	Program timing: Archer said the mission supports planned eVTOL Integration Pilot Program operations later in 2026.

•	Launch markets: The company is preparing for Los Angeles air-taxi operations tied to the LA28 Olympics and work in Texas, Florida, and New York.

•	Aircraft design: Midnight is designed to replace 60–90-minute car trips with electric flights.

$LLY said the FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy designation to olomorasib for previously treated, KRAS G12C-mutant advanced pancreatic cancer, based on preliminary Phase 1/2 LOXO-RAS-20001 data.

The Details:

•	Drug candidate: Olomorasib is an investigational next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor.

•	FDA pathway: Breakthrough Therapy designation is intended to expedite development and review of therapies for serious conditions.

•	Unmet need: Lilly said no approved targeted therapies currently exist for KRAS G12C-mutant pancreatic cancer.

$QBTS and Nasdaq Verafin will begin a proof of concept evaluating quantum-hybrid AI for financial-crime detection, with potential expansion into pilot programs.

The Details:

•	Technology: The initiative will use D-Wave’s annealing quantum technology with machine-learning applications.

•	Focus: The companies will assess detection of fraud, scams, and money laundering.

•	Data analysis: The proof of concept will analyze hundreds of data signals to improve predictive models.

•	Next steps: The collaboration could advance to pilot programs based on proof-of-concept results.

China’s CXMT is considering a second DRAM fabrication plant in Beijing’s Yizhuang technology hub while discussing financing with Beijing-backed technology investors.

The Details:

•	Funding: CXMT is reportedly seeking at least ¥60 million in local-government support for the proposed plant.

•	IPO: The expansion discussion follows CXMT’s reported $8.6 billion IPO last month.

•	Capacity: Expansion projects in Shanghai and Hefei could lift capacity above 600,000 wafers per month.

•	Industry backdrop: AI-infrastructure demand continues to support global memory-chip demand and supply constraints.

TSMC’s 3nm output is reportedly on track to reach 180,000 wafers per month in early Q4, ahead of its prior year-end target, amid strong demand from NVIDIA, AMD, and Broadcom.

The Details:

•	3nm ramp: Earlier reports projected 180,000 monthly 3nm wafers by year-end, up from roughly 120,000–130,000 at the end of 2025.

•	Demand drivers: AI chips from NVIDIA, AMD, and Broadcom are reported to be consuming advanced-node capacity.

•	2nm capacity: TSMC’s 2nm monthly output is projected to approach 100,000 wafers by year-end.

$TE agreed to supply Clearway with 641 MW of solar modules built with U.S.-made cells from T1’s planned G2_Austin facility.

The Details:

•	Module production: T1 will assemble the modules at its operational 5-GW G1_Dallas facility.

•	Cell supply: The modules will use solar cells manufactured at the planned 5-GW G2_Austin fab.

•	First phase: T1 previously projected the initial 2.1-GW G2_Austin phase would begin cell production by the end of 2026.

•	Domestic content: T1 expects to offer modules with more than 60% domestic content in 2027.

Morgan Stanley forecasts global cloud capital spending of $1.2 trillion in 2027, up 30% year over year and $170 billion above its pre-Q2 estimate.

The Details:

•	Capacity limits: The firm said all four major U.S. hyperscalers remain capacity constrained as AI demand outpaces supply.

•	Guidance changes: $GOOGL, $AMZN, and $META raised 2026 capex guidance, while $MSFT maintained its outlook.

•	Upside case: Morgan Stanley sees cloud capex potentially reaching $1.4 trillion.

•	Demand drivers: The forecast cites AI adoption, cloud demand, multiyear customer commitments, and improving infrastructure returns.

$NOC signed two multiyear framework agreements totaling more than $3 billion with the U.S. Department of War and $LMT to accelerate interceptor-component production.

The Details:

•	PAC-3 program: A $2 billion agreement covers solid rocket motors and ignition safety devices for Patriot Advanced Capability-3 Missile Segment Enhancement interceptors.

•	THAAD output: A $1 billion agreement will significantly increase monthly deliveries of Terminal High Altitude Area Defense components over seven years.

•	Facility capacity: Northrop is doubling Utah solid-rocket-motor capacity, nearly tripling capacity at Allegany Ballistics Lab, and increasing Elkton capacity by 25%.

•	Strategic purpose: The agreements support integrated air and missile defense and rising global demand for interceptor technologies.

$SHLS signed a strategic memorandum of understanding with TerraFlow Energy to support its grid-scale, long-duration energy-storage portfolio.

The Details:

•	Deployment scale: The MOU supports TerraFlow’s plan to deploy up to 5 GW of storage annually.

•	Shoals role: Shoals will provide power-distribution solutions for utility-scale and data-center applications.

•	Agreement status: The arrangement is a nonbinding strategic MOU.

•	Focus: The companies aim to expand infrastructure for long-duration energy storage.
$EDBL Edible Garden Secures Multi-Year Private Label Supply Agreement, Expanding Partnership with Major Midwest Big-Box Retailer

Bernstein raised its outlook for global server and AI GPU server shipments, projecting 15% and 22% annual growth through 2028. Raises AI server forecast to a $1 trillion market

The Details:

•	Server growth: Bernstein now sees global server shipments rising 15% annually.

•	AI GPUs: It expects AI GPU server shipments to grow 22% annually.

•	Market size: The firm projects the global server market will reach $1 trillion.

•	Cloud capex: Bernstein said 2026 capex forecasts for major cloud providers are up nearly 15% since March.

⁠Bernstein expects AI demand to keep server spending and data-center investment climbing.

Oracle’s 5-year credit default swap has climbed to about 215 basis points, a record level, indicating higher perceived default-insurance costs.

The Details:

•	Record level: The spread is said to be around 215 basis points.

•	Prior peak: That exceeds the previous high near 200 basis points from the Global Financial Crisis.

•	Meaning: A wider CDS spread means investors are paying more to insure Oracle debt against default.

⁠Oracle’s credit risk pricing has moved to a new record high.

$SPCX faces insider lock-up expirations starting Aug. 6, with about 20% of the locked shares initially becoming eligible for sale after its first earnings report.

The Details:

•	Initial unlock: Roughly 20% of the 180-day locked block becomes sellable at the first scheduled unlock.

•	Float growth: Staggered unlocks could expand the tradable float through late 2026.

•	Price backdrop: Shares have traded below the IPO price of $135.

•	Earnings timing: The company’s first earnings report is scheduled for Aug. 4, with lock-ups beginning to expire two days later.
